summary: hello-bat-fwi9 ships an obfuscated Windows dropper with Task Scheduler and sitecustomize.py persistence
details: The wheel ships a 2.5MB obfuscated hello.bat that is invoked by the package's advertised hello() function and by the hello-bat-fwi9 console_script. On Windows the batch launches a headless conhost, extracts a hidden CPython runtime to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python3_iFvHdqxj via tar.exe -xf python.zip, and decodes base64 fragments to write a sitecustomize.py into that runtime's site directory so every subsequent interpreter start re-executes the payload. Decoded fragments assemble a Python script that calls the Task Scheduler COM API (Schedule.Service / RegisterTaskDefinition) with SYSTEM/S4U logon fallbacks to install persistent scheduled-task execution, and contain CLR-hosting strings. The batch contains multi-megabyte base64 blobs (one ~1.8MB), scrambled environment-variable names, and set/call goto control-flow obfuscation. The README and METADATA explicitly claim the file is a readable 5-line hello.bat with no persistence, scheduled task, network access, or hidden execution — the shipped artifact performs the opposite, making the declared purpose a cover story. Running the advertised API on Windows yields full-host code execution and persistent compromise of the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
